title: The Galaxy
seo_title: Galaxy Charcuterie Board: Solar System Showpiece & Plan
description: A galaxy charcuterie board for 12 to 15: a brie sun, cheese ball planets with Parmesan rings and a burrata moon orbiting on black slate with dark fruit.
hook: A whole solar system on black slate: a brie sun, cheese ball planets and a burrata moon.

items.name: Cream cheese plus 8 oz sharp cheddar
Edible gold luster dust and gold star sprinkles

why: The planets are cheese balls in different coats, so each one looks different and tastes different. Grated Parmesan makes Saturn's rings, a whole brie is the sun and burrata is the moon.
Black grapes, blackberries and dark plums turn the slate into deep space, and bresaola, soppressata and salami fill the dark areas. It's a favorite for space-themed birthdays and New Year's Eve.

timeline.what: Make and roll the cheese-ball planets and bake the Parmesan rings. Store separately (the rings at room temperature, airtight).
Make the nebula swirl and set the sun.
Set the planets and the asteroid belt, then fill the dark field.

faq.q: How do you make cheese ball planets?
faq.a: Mix cream cheese and sharp cheddar, roll it into balls and give each one a different coating so they look like different planets.
A black slate or dark board, about 40 × 24 inches. The dark background is what makes it look like space.

Make the cheese ball planets the day before and keep them covered in the fridge. Keep meat, cheese and cut fruit out no more than 2 hours, or 1 hour above 90°F. For a long party, build half, keep the refill in the fridge and top it up halfway through.
